newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: British troops march to Argentine anthem.
newsitem.headline: British troops march to Argentine anthem.

text.p: British officers and soldiers competing in a skiing competition paraded on Monday as an Argentine military band played a march that calls for Argentine sovereignty over the British-held Falkland Islands.
The squad of British troops marched to the tune of "Malvinas Argentinas" before Argentine Defence Minister Jorge Dominguez in the southern Andean skiing resort of Bariloche.
Argentine army chief Gen. Martin Balza praised the British team for respecting their hosts' musical tastes.
"This is something that is part of army ceremony, and they respected that," he told the private DyN news agency, "It also shows the gentlemanly nature of the British soldier."
He merely smiled when asked why "Malvinas Argentinas" was selected for the parade, DyN reported.

Argentina has disputed the sovereignty of the islands it calls the Malvinas with Britain for more than 160 years. In 1982 a military junta sent a force to snatch control of the South Atlantic archipelago. Britain then won a 10-week war, in which about 1,000 troops, mainly Argentines, were killed.
Relations between the two countries slowly warmed after the return of Argentine democracy in 1983, and diplomatic ties were reestablished after President Carlos Menem took office in 1989.
The British soldiers were in Argentina to compete in a skiing competition for mountain troops against teams from Argentina, Chile, the United States, France and Italy.
